To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) CPXV is an emerging pathogen that can cause severe generalized infection in banded mongoos and jaguarundies, (2) CPXV can be transmitted from rodents to other animals via feeding, (3) CPXV transmission can occur between animals of the same species and between animals of different species and (4) CPXV infection of humans can be caused by contact with infected animals or their bedding.
CPXV infections can occur in a time-delayed manner in different animal species and geographical areas.

CPXV is not only an emerging zoonosis but also an emerging pathogen for exotic animals in zoos, which may lead to a time-delayed infection in humans, and that CPXV infections are on the rise in Germany.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new CPXV host species and their role in the epidemiology and zoonotic transmission.
the detection and analysis of CPXV in animals and humans, as well as the identification and characterization of new CPXV strains.
the detection and characterization of CPXV in a variety of hosts and the identification of potential risk factors for the transmission of this zoonotic virus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the risk of CPXV infection in man is increasing and that this risk is underestimated.
CPXV is not as rare as it is often described.
the CPXV is a virus with a broad host spectrum and that it is a virus that is still able to adapt to new hosts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CPXV is a highly zoonotic and potentially dangerous pathogen.
a CPXV infection in an exotic mammal can be the starting point of an outbreak and a source for human infection.

the CPXV outbreak in this zoo was caused by a virus strain that was transmitted to the zoo via food rats, which were infected with a CPXV strain that was circulating in the wild rodent population in the region of origin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a CPXV outbreak in a zoo can have serious implications for the general public.
CPXV infections are on the rise and that the list of animals that are susceptible to CPX virus infections is growing.
a thorough risk assessment is required in order to avoid future outbreaks of CPXV in exotic animals and to protect the public.
